summary: The root شَمَخَ (shamakh) primarily describes something high or lofty, like a mountain. It also refers to pride, specifically elevating one's nose in disdain.
lane: جَبَلٌ شَامِخٌ ذ A high, or lofty, mountain; (S, A, L;) as also [but in an intensive sense, i. e. a very high or lofty mountain]: (L:) pl. جِبَالٌ شَوَامِخُ (S, A) and شُمَّخٌ . (A.) -b2- Hence, شَامِخٌ signifies also Proud; (L, TA;) elevating the nose, from pride, or disdain: [like زَامِخٌ :] pl. شُمَّخٌ : (L, K:) and a man who magnifies, or exalts, himself much; or elevates his nose much, from pride. (L.) -b3- And أُنُوفٌ شُمَّخٌ [ Noses elevated, from pride ]; like زُمَّخٌ . (S.) -b4- And نَسَبٌ شَامِخٌ (tropical:) [ A proud, or high, lineage ]. (TA.)
